purpose: Five authored, fictional Grade 5 assignments for an inspectable teacher-controlled demonstration. Prepared readings are not live-model evaluations.

fixtureUsage.liveMode: Extraction receives the uploaded image, template prompts, question IDs, objective IDs, criteria and known page regions. It never receives these reference writtenAnswer values, expected findings, intended groups, correction targets, or future follow-up answers.
fixtureUsage.reasoningInput: Use the actual extracted transcript and teacher corrections, known question/rubric context, recorded support, deterministic arithmetic checks, current lesson and constraints. Do not feed intended scenario categories or expected grouping as student evidence.
fixtureUsage.fixturePlayback: May seed the reference transcripts and explicitly labeled simulated extraction for offline development or recording a disclosed replay. Every seeded/replayed result must show fixture provenance and must not be presented as a successful live model call.
fixtureUsage.groundTruth: Expected answers, reference writtenAnswer values, actual support, intended scenarios and expected outcomes are instructor/test ground truth. The answer key may be used by deterministic arithmetic checks and teacher materials; it does not prove a student's work or interpretation.
fixtureUsage.support: Independence is a teacher-recorded task condition, never an inference from correct work. A correction adds an audit event and revises interpretation without replacing the original scan.
fixtureUsage.typedMath: validationKind distinguishes fraction-addition, construct-addition, and explanation. Fixed operands and expected rationals are instructor/checker data, not student evidence. Canonical strings are retained for display. Do not infer open-response correctness by matching the examplePairs verbatim.
fixtureUsage.comparisonLimit: Tasks, difficulty and help differ. These authored examples are not a validated growth measure or a real classroom study.

unit.title: Adding fractions with unlike denominators
unit.scope: Positive proper fractions, unlike denominators, sums at most one; no mixed numbers.
unit.prerequisiteRule: Prerequisites describe planned curriculum exposure and within-lesson content order, not permanent student mastery. Preserve the authored unit sequence; targeted support may revisit prerequisites inside a concurrent block.

learningObjectives.description: Represent equivalent fractions as the same quantity using equal-sized wholes.
Add fractions with unlike denominators by rewriting them in a common fractional unit.
Explain a fraction-addition word problem with working, a reasonable total, and appropriate units.

assessmentCriteria.description: Rewrite fractions without changing their values; fraction models must use equal-sized wholes.
Express addends in a common fractional unit before adding.
Add numerators and retain the common denominator; accept mathematically equivalent unreduced answers.
Show enough calculation steps, a labeled model, or a clear explanation to inspect the method.
For word problems, interpret the total with the stated unit.

Calculate 1/4 + 2/3. Show your equivalent fractions and the sum.
Calculate 2/5 + 1/10. Show your steps. You may simplify your answer.
A class uses 3/8 meter of ribbon for one display and 1/4 meter for another. How many meters of ribbon does it use altogether? Show your working and include the unit.

followupQuestions.prompt: Calculate 1/3 + 1/4. Show equivalent fractions or an equal-whole model that explains your answer.

targeted.title: Equal parts before adding

prompts.prompt: Use two equal-length fraction strips. Shade 1/2 on one and 1/4 on the other. Rename the halves as fourths, then find 1/2 + 1/4.
prompts.answerKey: 1/2 = 2/4; 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4. The strips must represent the same-sized whole.

prompts.prompt: Draw or use equal-length strips to solve 1/5 + 1/10. Label the equal-sized parts and write the matching calculation.
A fictional student says 1/2 + 1/4 = 2/6 because they added both tops and bottoms. Explain what needs to change, then write a correct calculation.
prompts.answerKey: Halves and fourths are different-sized parts. Rename 1/2 as 2/4 and add 2/4 + 1/4 = 3/4. The answer 2/6 is smaller than 1/2, so it cannot be the sum of these positive addends.

teacherPrompts: Are both wholes the same size?
What kind of part are we counting?
Can we rename the fractions without changing their values?
targeted.scaffolds: Provide equal-length blank fraction bars and strips divided into fourths and tenths. Record hints or worked examples as support for this activity.

independentEntryCheck.conditions: No hints, worked examples, or peer help; record any actual assistance.
independentEntryCheck.nextAction: Teacher inspects what was shown and selects application or additional information gathering; no runtime automatic reassignment during teaching is required.
independentEntryCheck.title: Independent entry check

prompts.prompt: A class uses 1/4 meter of blue ribbon and 1/5 meter of green ribbon. Find the total length. Show working.
One plant grows 1/5 meter in a month and another 1/2 meter in the same month. How much growth is that altogether? Show working.

independentApplication.note: Students who do not need an entry check may spend the whole 12-minute block on application and explaining their methods.
independentApplication.title: Independent application

prompts.prompt: Solve 1/4 + 2/5 using twentieths and again using fortieths. Explain why the answers have the same value.
Write two different pairs of positive fractions with unlike denominators that add to 3/4. Prove each pair works.
Explain why adding the denominators does not count equal-sized parts. Use one of your calculations as evidence.
prompts.answerKey: An explanation should connect denominator to part size, rename unlike units into the same unit, and retain that denominator when adding numerators.

exit.title: What kind of part are we counting?

prompts.prompt: Calculate 1/4 + 1/6. Show how you use equal-sized parts.
Finish the sentence: Before adding, I rewrite the fractions because…
prompts.answerKey: Accept an explanation that the fractions need the same-sized parts/common unit before their counts can be added.
